subject: Reserved capacity proposal - Tailwind AI (commit term & discount approval)
messages:
From: Ava Grant <ava@tailwind.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>; Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Oct 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity ask — term flexibility and discount

Hi Sofia / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the Tailwind team is excited about Redwood's latency and cost profile for embeddings and chat. We're running an internal sizing exercise and have a draft committed request that would cover our production forecast for 12 months: 600 A100-equivalent GPU hours/month reserved (phased activation).

Couple of asks we need clarified to move to procurement:
- Can Redwood support a 14-month commit term (12 months of billing + 2 months of activation buffer) without changing the base discount structure?
- Because our model footprint is sensitive to GPU spot market movement, we need a >15% blended discount to make the unit economics work for our board. Is there scope for an exception or an approval path?

I've attached a short workbook with our forecast and a draft SLA we plan to use for legal. Happy to jump on a call.

Best,
Ava Grant
Head of Infrastructure, Tailwind AI
ava@tailwind.ai

Attachments: tailwind_commit_workbook.xlsx (referenced), draft_SLA_tailwind.pdf (referenced)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Oct 2025 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — term flexibility and discount

Hi Ava / Liam —

Thanks for sharing the forecast — good level of detail and that phased approach makes sense operationally. Quick answers up front:
- We can support a 14-month operational window (12 paid + 2 activation months) as a special setup; ops will need a phased provisioning plan.
- Our standard reserved-capacity discount bands top out at around 12% for this sizing. Anything beyond that requires finance sign-off and usually a deal-level concession (e.g., non-cancellable tranche, minimum utilization SLAs, or partial pass-through).

I'll loop in Finance and Solutions with a proposed structure. To keep momentum, attached is a short draft of a commit term (pricing/activation schedule + SOW). Would you be able to confirm a target blended discount number (is 16–18% the board ask)?

If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-min alignment this week.

Cheers,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Marcus / Karthik —

Forwarding Tailwind's ask. TL;DR: Tailwind is targeting a 14-month commit (12 paid + 2 activation) at ~600 A100-eq hrs/month. They indicated they need >15% blended discount to proceed (board threshold). Our standard top-band is ~12% for this size.

Request: can Finance approve a one-time concession to reach 16% blended discount if we include: 1) non-cancellable first 8 months, 2) a utilization SLA (>=70% monthly avg), and 3) a 1% escrow holdback for GPU-price swing protection? We'd also ask Solutions (Karthik) to confirm operational feasibility for phased activation schedule.

Why it matters: Tailwind is a strategic ISV in our mid-market PLG motion; win helps sector credibility and could seed a Dedicated landing. Without an approval path, they'll likely push procurement to other vendors.

I've attached the draft commit we shared. I can patch in the conditions if Finance wants them.

Best,
Sofia

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>; Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Oct 2025 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Tailwind — reserved capacity: pricing sensitivity (need approval)

Sofia — thanks for the context and the workbook. Quick read and recommendation below.

Summary: 600 A100-eq / month x 12 paid months (~7,200 A100-eq hours) is material but within our mid-market band. A straight 16% unblock would be outside delegation for Sales leadership — requires either VP Finance sign-off or a structured trade. I'll approve up to 15% with the following binding conditions to protect Redwood economics:

1) Non-cancellable tranche for first 8 months (billing begins month 1).
2) Minimum utilization SKU SLA: 70% of reserved capacity monthly averaged over rolling 3 months, else tailwind pays shortfall for underutilized hours at 60% of list.
3) GPU-price pass-through floor: if average GPU spot-equivalent cost rises >12% vs baseline, Redwood can adjust pricing for new months with 30 days notice.
4) Redwood retains right to convert portion of reserved capacity to preemptible/ burst credits during defined maintenance windows — will not affect committed billable hours but preserves ops flexibility.

If Tailwind accepts those conditions, Finance signs off on 15% blended discount. If Sales wants 16–18%, we need Exec approval and a documented business case (strategic value, reference potential, and uplift to ARR).

Action: Sofia — propose I draft the concession language and Karthik to confirm implementation. Marissa — if you want the higher band, submit a short exec memo (why >15%) and I'll route.

Marcus Lin
Director, Finance — Revenue & Pricing
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
